status_summary: On 2025-02-01 Executive Order 14193 imposed duties on Canadian goods with energy resources at 10 percent rather than 25 percent, a measure that taxed cross-border energy trade, and Executive Order 14389 of 2026-02-20 ended those IEEPA duties. The National Security Strategy released 2025-12-04 calls for building resilient energy infrastructure with regional partners. Executive Order 14373 of 2026-01-09 placed Venezuelan oil revenue funds under US custody and OFAC General License 46 of 2026-01-29 authorized certain Venezuelan-origin oil activities by established US companies under conditions, and on 2026-04-30 a Presidential Permit authorized Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC to build a 36-inch crude oil border pipeline in Phillips County, Montana.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14193 (90 FR 9113), signed 2025-02-01, imposed an additional 25 percent duty on products of Canada, with energy and energy resources subject to 10 percent instead, effective 2025-02-04.

The White House released the National Security Strategy (cover dated November 2025), whose Western Hemisphere section calls for building scalable and resilient energy infrastructure with regional governments and businesses and which ranks energy dominance as a strategic priority; it has no Canada- or Mexico-specific energy passage.

Executive Order 14373 (91 FR 2045) declared a national emergency over judicial process against funds from Venezuelan natural resource sales held in the United States, barring attachment of those funds absent a license, and treated them as Venezuelan sovereign property in US custody to be disbursed as the Secretary of State directs, with the Treasury Secretary to consult the Energy Secretary on management.
OFAC issued Venezuela-related General License 46, Authorizing Certain Activities Involving Venezuelan-Origin Oil; per a law-firm alert it covers trade by established US companies under conditions.
timeline.source: U.S. Department of the Treasury, OFAC

timeline.event: Executive Order 14389 (91 FR 9437) ended the additional IEEPA duties imposed under nine earlier orders, including EO 14193 on Canadian goods; it states that duties under section 232 and section 301 are not affected.

The President issued a Presidential Permit to Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC to construct, connect, operate and maintain a 36-inch crude oil and petroleum products pipeline at the US-Canada border in Phillips County, Montana (91 FR 24333, published 2026-05-05), on an application of 2026-01-30.

title: Hemisphere-focused energy policy with Mexico, Canada and others to raise production
uncertainties: Executive Order 14389 ended the EO 14193 duties and states that section 232 and section 301 duties are unaffected; whether any such duties apply to Canadian energy was not checked. Mexico energy policy, LNG export approvals and Canadian electricity were not researched. The Keystone XL link comes from trade press; the permit itself names only Bridger Pipeline Expansion LLC. The blocker on Canada talks and the USMCA review status rest on a law firm alert. Whether Venezuelan oil licensing is a hemisphere-focused energy policy in the Mandate's sense is a judgment call. Primary lift: the text of General License 46 could not be read (the OFAC page lists it without text), so its conditions rest on the law-firm alert. The permit was signed by the President, not the Secretary of State. No document describing a joint hemisphere energy policy was found, and the record's match remains a loose parallel. Independent review of 2026-10-16: the National Security Strategy carries only a November 2025 cover date; the 2025-12-04 release date rests on a law-firm summary, and the page numbers cited earlier were dropped because printed and PDF numbering differ. The OFAC recent-actions page confirms General License 46 and its title but not its terms. Executive Order 14193 states an effective date of 2025-02-04; later changes to its timing were not checked.
